solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: What better hopes for replacing those with influence?

indicators.note: the letters of the first three words are put back in a new order, replacing the old arrangement

explanation.surface: A punter wonders what to wish for in place of the people currently in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for replacing' signals the anagram of WHAT BETTER HOPES; 'better' is a gambler here, not a comparative.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for the authorities, the people who hold power and sway over others.

clue.text: Naturally fitted for role like Hamlet

definitions.meaning: suited by birth and upbringing to a position, as if born into it
Hamlet uses this very phrase of himself in Shakespeare's play, and he was born a prince

explanation.walkthrough: 'role' works twice: a position in life, and the theatrical part of Hamlet, who speaks the phrase in Act 1.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for someone at ease in a position because birth prepared them for it, as Hamlet says of Danish customs.

clue.text: European nations and lands for development

parts.note: states are nations

explanation.surface: Europe's countries and the territory they plan to build on.
explanation.definitionFit: Housing or industrial estates are tracts of land set aside to be developed.

clue.text: After massage R. Laver ego too big?

indicators.note: a massage works and kneads, so the letters that follow are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: After a rubdown, has tennis great Rod Laver's self-regard swollen out of proportion?
explanation.walkthrough: R. Laver is Rod Laver, the Australian tennis champion; 'After massage' is the rearrangement signal, not a time marker.
explanation.definitionFit: Something oversized is simply bigger than it should be, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Given relief when caught in river's back-flow

indicators.note: one piece is trapped inside the other, like a fish caught in a current
a flow running backwards, so the river's name is read in reverse

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and another on the England-Wales border
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Someone is comforted after being swept into a river's backwash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back-flow' turns the river's name to EED, and 'caught in' traps the word for 'when' within it.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease pain is to relieve it, so someone given relief has been eased.

clue.text: Liveliness with power to be for Sarkozy an explosive component

parts.note: salt can mean wit or piquancy, a lively quality
P is the abbreviation for power in physics
former French president Sarkozy would say 'etre' for 'to be'

explanation.surface: A French president is credited with spirit and the power to be explosive.
explanation.walkthrough: Nicolas Sarkozy, a French president, points to the French verb etre.
explanation.definitionFit: Potassium nitrate is the oxidising ingredient in gunpowder, alongside charcoal and sulphur.

clue.text: Seaside city Mafia henchmen hold up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top
the two words hold the city's name within their letters

explanation.surface: Gangsters' heavies are robbing a coastal city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold' finds AIFAH across MAFIA HENCHMEN and 'up' turns it round; 'hold up' looks like a robbery.
explanation.definitionFit: Haifa is Israel's main port on the Mediterranean coast, so a city by the sea.

clue.text: One into peculiar nature of organic compound

indicators.note: one piece goes into the middle of the other
peculiar means odd or strange, so the letters are oddly arranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: One digs into the strange character of a chemical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peculiar' scrambles NATURE to TAURNE, and 'into' puts I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Taurine is an amino acid derivative found in bile and energy drinks, an organic chemical.

clue.text: The renowned Navy messed up occasionally

indicators.note: something messed up is disordered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: The famous Royal Navy blundered from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'messed up' rearranges all fifteen letters of THE RENOWNED NAVY.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means at irregular intervals, from time to time.

clue.text: Nervous laughter where teetotaller in bank takes shilling

indicators.note: the abstainer goes inside the row

parts.note: a bank of seats is a tier
TT is short for teetotal, someone who drinks no alcohol
S was the abbreviation for the old British shilling coin

explanation.surface: A nondrinker in a row of seats is paid a shilling, prompting giggles.
explanation.walkthrough: The shilling was a pre-decimal British coin, abbreviated S; 'takes' just adds it.
explanation.definitionFit: Titters are suppressed, nervous giggles, a near synonym for anxious laughing.

clue.text: Euler is prepared for retirement

indicators.note: the letters are made ready in a new form, as food is prepared

explanation.surface: The mathematician Euler is ready to stop working.
explanation.walkthrough: Euler was an 18th-century Swiss mathematician; 'prepared' rearranges EULER IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Retirement means withdrawal from work into free time, a sense shared by leisure.

clue.text: Lavishly praise former Time Lord making comeback in Doctor's absence

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: coming back means turning round, so the trimmed word is read backwards
the doctor, abbreviated Dr, is absent, so the letters D and R are dropped from the word Lord

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Doctor Who fan gushes over a former Time Lord returning without the Doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Doctor's absence' leaves LO once the abbreviation Dr is gone, and 'making comeback' turns it to OL; the Time Lord is from Doctor Who.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise enthusiastically, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: During divinity pray endlessly against moral turpitude

indicators.note: the pieces fall during, so within, the god

parts.note: a divinity is a deity, a god

indicators.note: the word pray loses its final letter

parts.note: V for versus means against

explanation.surface: Praying in a divinity class is set against wickedness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims the prayer word to three letters, and 'During' places them, with V for versus, inside the word for a god.
explanation.definitionFit: Turpitude is depraved wickedness, so depravity is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Soaking for sailor, very corrupt, receiving rand

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman

indicators.note: the following pair takes in another letter between them

parts.note: so means very, as in 'so tired'
bent is slang for corrupt or dishonest
R is the abbreviation for the South African rand

explanation.surface: A seaman, thoroughly crooked, pockets South African money.
explanation.walkthrough: The rand is South Africa's currency; 'receiving' sets its letter between the words for 'very' and 'corrupt'.
explanation.definitionFit: Absorbent material takes up liquid, the adjectival sense of soaking up.

clue.text: Noun operates differently in composite language

indicators.note: the letters are arranged differently from how they appear

parts.note: N is the grammatical abbreviation for noun
taken as written

explanation.surface: A noun functions in a new way within a mixed language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'differently' rearranges N and OPERATES.
explanation.definitionFit: Esperanto is an invented language built from roots drawn from many European tongues.

clue.text: Communist in firm belief

indicators.note: the communist sits inside the company

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
a red is a communist

explanation.surface: A party member has a strong conviction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' looks like an adjective for the belief but is a company, CO.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a statement of one's principles or faith, from Latin for 'I believe'.

clue.text: Boy singer with his rector for excitement

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: A choirboy and his vicar are getting worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for excitement' rearranges HIS RECTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A chorister is a member of a church choir, often a boy treble.

clue.text: From Scandinavia (and not some London district)

parts.note: nor means and not
SE is the postcode area for south-east London

explanation.surface: A bracketed note excludes a part of London from being Nordic.
explanation.walkthrough: London postcodes use compass letters, so SE is the south-east district.
explanation.definitionFit: Norse describes the old peoples and language of Norway and Scandinavia generally.

clue.text: Scientist associated with groundbreaking research?

parts.note: groundbreaking is read literally as the ground breaking in an earthquake, whose strength the seismologist's scale measures

explanation.walkthrough: Charles Richter devised the scale for earthquake magnitude in 1935; 'groundbreaking' means innovative on the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The American seismologist gave his name to the scale measuring earthquakes.

clue.text: Formless poem, Anne Hathaway's first, observed events

indicators.note: without form, so the letters lose their order and are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: only the initial letter of the surname is used

explanation.surface: A shapeless verse by Shakespeare's wife Anne Hathaway was seen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' takes H from Hathaway; 'Formless' rearranges POEM, ANNE and H.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenomena are facts or events that can be seen or perceived, the plural of phenomenon.

clue.text: Wood maintains it is goverment (sic) by chosen group

indicators.note: the tree holds the words in, maintaining them inside

parts.note: elm is a kind of wood
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dictionary entry with a typo flagged as rule by an elite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maintains' puts IT IS inside ELM; '(sic)' just flags the misspelling 'goverment'.
explanation.definitionFit: Elitism is the belief that a select few should rule or hold privilege, government by an elect.

clue.text: People seen with heroin runner

parts.note: a race is a people or ethnic group
horse is old slang for heroin

explanation.surface: Folk are spotted with a hard drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' suggests a drug courier, but it is a horse running in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: A racehorse runs in races, so runner is a racing word for one.

clue.text: Lyttelton's dissatisfied exclamation?

definitions.meaning: Humphrey Lyttelton, the British jazz trumpeter and radio host, was known by this nickname
a grunt of displeasure or doubt

explanation.walkthrough: Humphrey Lyttelton was a jazz trumpeter and host of BBC radio's 'I'm Sorry I Haven't a Clue', always called by the shortened name.
explanation.definitionFit: The interjection is a grunt of scepticism, and also the nickname of a famous jazzman.

clue.text: Man United ditching complete system get three points

indicators.note: to ditch is to get rid of, so the letters of the system are dropped

parts.note: a unit is a complete whole or self-contained system
a win earns three points in a football league

explanation.surface: Manchester United abandon their whole system yet earn a victory.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing UNIT from UNITED leaves ED; 'Man United' pretends to be the football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Edwin is a male first name, so a man in crossword terms.

clue.text: Old story line in the eleventh year after Christ?

indicators.note: the line goes inside the date

parts.note: the year 11 AD, with the digits 11 read as the letters I I

explanation.surface: A tale set in the early first century.
explanation.walkthrough: The numeral 11 is read as two letter Is, giving IIAD; L goes in after the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epic of the Trojan War is a very ancient tale.

clue.text: Turkish dynasty created in books given to us

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible
to man, with man meaning humankind, us as a species

explanation.surface: An Ottoman line is formed from scripture handed down to humanity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' and 'created in' are joining words; 'us' is humankind, MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ottomans ruled the Turkish empire from about 1300 to 1922.

clue.text: Rather feeble compilers finally get this sorted

parts.note: setters refer to themselves as we

indicators.note: only the last letter of the word get is used
the letters are sorted into a new order

explanation.surface: The setters at last get this weak effort put right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes T from GET and 'sorted' rearranges THIS to TISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Wet means feeble or ineffectual in British slang, and the -ish ending makes it rather so.

clue.text: Maybe Geordie and Tony turn on charm somehow

indicators.note: in some way or other, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Newcastle lad and Tony somehow switch on the charm.
explanation.walkthrough: A Geordie is someone from Newcastle upon Tyne in north-east England; 'somehow' rearranges TONY TURN ON CHARM.
explanation.definitionFit: A Geordie is one example of someone from the north of England.
